articles.title: 'Punishment that sends shiver down the team': Ex-England captain on Brydon Carse nightclub incident
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former England captain Michael Vaughan has called for a severe punishment following Brydon Carseâs latest involvement in a nightclub incident, saying .
articles.body: Former England captain Michael Vaughan has called for a severe punishment following Brydon Carseâs latest involvement in a nightclub incident, saying the ECB must take action strong enough to deter the entire England cricket setup from similar behaviour.Carse became the latest England player to attract scrutiny after a video emerged showing the fast bowler handcuffed by police outside a nightclub. He was briefly arrested while out with Durham team-mates Ben Stokes and Matthew Potts, leading the England and Wales Cricket Board to investigate the incident.Carse had been part of Englandâs squad for two of the three Tests against Pakistan but was released to play for Durham after being left out of the XI for the first Test at Leeds. He contributed 26 runs and returned figures of 2-82 as Durham beat Derbyshire inside three days.The 30-year-old then went out with his Durham team-mates to celebrate the victory, during which the incident occurred.The ECB subsequently confirmed that Carse âwill no longer be available for selectionâ for the second Test against Pakistan at Lordâs on Thursday. Hampshire right-arm seamer Sonny Baker has been called up as his replacement.Vaughan believes the latest episode requires a response that sends a clear message across English cricket."Someone is going to have to get a punishment that sends a shiver down the whole England cricket team and right down through the programme, so that everyone knows that if you misbehave or bring any kind of bad reputation on to this team, you know what's going to come," former England captain Vaughan said on BBC Radio. "It's the only punishment that will really hurt players."Carseâs case comes amid a series of off-field incidents involving England players over the past year. Last October, white-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer outside a nightclub in Wellington, New Zealand, while Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue were also present.During the Ashes tour of Australia, Ben Duckett was filmed apparently drunk during Englandâs holiday in Noosa.Then, in June, former Test captain Ben Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and were present when a member of Englandâs security staff was punched by Saracens rugby player in a London nightclub.Vaughan acknowledged that Carse could feel hard done by if he is punished heavily in light of the wider pattern of incidents."I hope Carse is getting good support around him. He is a character who can be a little bit loose and if you give him a bit of rope he'll take a huge amount of it. He needs people around him who are giving him better advice."I would feel for Carse if he is the one who takes the rap for what has happened over the past nine months, but somewhere, somehow, something has to be done to set a precedent that they won't stand for that behaviour any more," said Vaughan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Batting failure? No problem: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits back with two wickets in four balls in Duleep Trophy - WATCH
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: A poor outing with the bat did not stop Vaibhav Sooryavanshi from making an impact in the Duleep Trophy. The 15-year-old East Zone vice-cap.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A poor outing with the bat did not stop Vaibhav Sooryavanshi from making an impact in the Duleep Trophy. The 15-year-old East Zone vice-captain rolled up his sleeves and picked up two wickets in the space of four balls against North East Zone in the quarter-final at the BCCI Centre of Excellence Ground 2 in Bengaluru.Sooryavanshi had faced only six balls and scored eight runs before being dismissed by North East Zone pacer Bishworjit Konthoujam in East Zone's first innings. But he responded with the ball, needing only eight deliveries to take his first wicket.Two wickets in four ballsSooryavanshi claimed his third first-class wicket with the second delivery of the 28th over. He bowled a three-quarter-length delivery outside off and Kishan Lyngdoh came down the track to attack. Lyngdoh swung hard but lost his shape and got a leading edge towards cover. Substitute fielder Denish Das completed a safe catch.Three balls later, Sooryavanshi struck again. He bowled a good-length delivery around off stump to Imliwati Lemtur, who defended from the crease. The batter got a thin outside edge and wicketkeeper Ishan Kishan reacted quickly to take a sharp catch.âYou've got to be patientâFormer India head coach Rahul Dravid has called for patience with Sooryavanshi, saying the young batter will need time and enough red-ball cricket to develop in the longest format."With Vaibhav, you've got to be patient. He's only 15-years-old, and from what I've seen of the kid, I have no doubt that given the opportunity to practice and play domestic cricket and a couple of seasons of red-ball cricket, he will be able to hold his own in a Test match team," Dravid said on JioStar.Dravid said Sooryavanshi's busy schedule with the Indian team could make it difficult for him to find enough time to play full domestic seasons."Whether he'll be able to break into the eleven with the guys already performing, that's a different story and a tricky one.""Whether he'll have the time to play two full seasons of domestic cricket because he'll be so busy playing for India in the white-ball format, I'm not sure about that. So skill-wise, I think no problem; whether they'll be able to do it because of schedules might be a bit more tricky," Dravid said.Red-ball work still in progressSooryavanshi has already achieved plenty at the age of 15, but red-ball cricket remains an area where he is still developing. He made his first-class debut for Bihar in January 2024 at the age of 12. In eight first-class matches, he has scored 207 runs at an average of 17.25, with one half-century.However, Sooryavanshi has already enjoyed remarkable success in white-ball cricket. He scored 439 runs at the 2026 U-19 World Cup before producing a stunning IPL season for Rajasthan Royals. He smashed 776 runs in 16 matches at a strike rate of 237.31, hit 72 sixes and won the Orange Cap and MVP award.Sooryavanshi then made his senior India debut in July 2026 and impressed immediately in T20Is. The left-hander scored 151 runs in three matches against Zimbabwe at a strike rate of 196.10, including 81 off 49 balls. He also won the Player of the Series award as India completed a 2-0 series sweep.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Zeeshan Ansari: 'India A and IPL exposure has made me a better leg-spinner'
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Zeeshan Ansari went six years in cricket's red-ball wilderness. After playing for Uttar Pradesh against Tamil Nadu in the Ranji Trophy in J.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Zeeshan Ansari went six years in cricket's red-ball wilderness. After playing for Uttar Pradesh against Tamil Nadu in the Ranji Trophy in January 2020, the legspinner admitted that he found it difficult to bowl with the red cherry. The influx of T20 competitions had accustomed him to the white ball over the red.That time away ended when the 26-year-old earned a surprise call-up to the India A squad for the Sri Lanka tour. The comeback didn't get a dream Bollywood-esque start. He gave away 76 runs in 19 overs in the first innings in Galle. He was then hammered for 29 runs in the four overs he bowled in the second essay.The Lucknow-born leggie admitted that the comeback had been a 'little difficult'. He sees this as a learning curve, with the exposure making him a better bowler."It was a good learning experience. I played red-ball cricket after so many years, and I got to learn a lot. There were a lot of good batsmen I was bowling against. The Sri Lankan batters are good players of spin. And I was also bowling with the Kookaburra ball for the first time. It was a different experience for me," he says.Interestingly, Zeeshan had garnered attention early in his career because of his exploits with the red ball. At the U-19 Cooch Behar Trophy in 2014-15, the UP player took 40 wickets, which helped him get into the 2016 U-19 World Cup squad. He picked up 30 wickets in the CK Nayudu Trophy in 2016-17 and was rewarded immediately as he was selected for the Ranji Trophy the following year. He made an impressive debut under the captaincy of Suresh Raina. Zeeshan picked up six wickets in the match but was dropped for the next fixture. In the next four seasons, he played four more games until 2020, before he was left in the wilderness.Gautam (Gambhir) sir just told me that I am doing well and should keep bowling like this, just as I have been. There is nothing else to think about.Then, earlier this year, he got a surprise call-up first as a net bowler for the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Chandigarh, followed by his India A selection. A day before the Test match against Afghanistan, Ansari was seen having a long conversation with Team India head coach Gautam Gambhir."Gautam sir just told me that I am doing well and should keep bowling like this, just as I have been. There is nothing else to think about. Just keep performing. It was a good conversation, and it boosted my confidence," he recalls.The exposure, Zeeshan feels, has made him a better bowler, and he has learnt more about his bowling and what exactly he needs to do to find more success."I have now played in the IPL, gone with India A, met a lot of people and worked with some really good coaches. All of that has helped me understand my cricket better and learn what can work for me and what I need to do to be successful. For instance, I have realised that I need to bowl a little slower and put more revs on the ball. I have kept that in mind, and that is what I am working on," he says."I learnt that you should bowl as much as you can with the red ball. Whatever variations you have, you should work on them well and then try to execute them in matches. The most important thing is repetition. Repetition is very important for a leg-spinner. I have practised so much that I am now able to bring variations into my googlies as well," he adds.I feel my career has been made because of the UPT20 League. I wasn't playing much cricket and my name wasn't known anywhere.Zeeshan, who plays for Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) in the Indian Premier League (IPL), credits the UP T20 League for giving his career a new lease of life."I feel my career has been made because of the UPT20 League. I wasn't playing much cricket and my name wasn't known anywhere. In the first season of the league, I won the Purple Cap with 24 wickets to my name, and that's when people started recognising me," he says.Zeeshan is still 26 and now, with selectors tracking his development closely, he will hopefully get more chances for his state team. This time around, he won't have to live in the wilderness.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Duleep Trophy: Shahbaz Ahmed shines as East Zone thrash North East Zone to enter semis
articles.summary: Cricket News: Shahbaz Ahmedâs commanding 167 and Anukul Royâs five-wicket haul powered East Zone to an innings-and-210-run victory over North East Zone in the Dulee.
articles.body: Shahbaz Ahmedâs commanding 167 and Anukul Royâs five-wicket haul powered East Zone to an innings-and-210-run victory over North East Zone in the Duleep Trophy quarterfinal at the BCCI Centre of Excellence Ground 2 on Tuesday.East Zone first posted a massive 467 before Abhijit Sarkarâs five-wicket haul helped dismiss North East Zone for 111 in their first innings. Forced to follow on, North East Zone were bowled out for 146, with Anukul claiming five wickets as East Zone completed a dominant win.Shahbaz, Gharami build huge totalShahbaz was at the centre of East Zoneâs big first-innings total, scoring 167 off 244 balls with 17 fours and four sixes. Sudip Kumar Gharami also played a major role, hitting 146 off 185 balls, with 25 fours and a six.East Zone had slipped to 138 for five, but Gharami and Shahbaz put the innings back on track with a crucial partnership. Shahbaz continued to take the team towards a commanding total even after Gharami was dismissed.East Zone eventually finished on 467 in 112.5 overs.Sarkar sparks collapseNorth East Zone struggled to deal with East Zoneâs bowling attack and were bowled out for 111 in 42.5 overs.Sarkar was the pick of the bowlers, returning impressive figures of 5-20 in 9.5 overs. Shahbaz also made a significant contribution with 3-20.Arpit Bhatewara top-scored with 32, while captain Rongsen Jonathan made 21. The rest of the North East Zone batting line-up failed to put up much resistance.Anukul completes the jobForced to follow on, North East Zone were soon in trouble again at 10 for one. Pheiroijam Jotin offered some resistance with 39, while Akash Choudhary scored 27 and Kishan Lyngdoh made 25.Anukul then took charge of the attack, finishing with 5-37 from 15 overs. Youngster Vaibhav Sooryavanshi also impressed with two wickets, while Mukesh Kumar and Sarkar picked up one each.North East Zone were eventually dismissed for 146 in 50 overs, handing East Zone a comprehensive innings-and-210-run victory.Shami looks for better outingWhile the younger bowlers impressed with disciplined lengths and regular breakthroughs, East Zoneâs most experienced pacer Mohammed Shami had a quiet outing.The India quick went wicketless in both innings and will be hoping for a stronger performance when East Zone return to action in the semifinal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India vs Sri Lanka: Colombo Test sees third ICC punishment as Jayasuriya joins Jaiswal, Fernando
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka spinner Prabath Jayasuriya has become the third player to be officially sanctioned during the ongoing second Test against India i.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka spinner Prabath Jayasuriya has become the third player to be officially sanctioned during the ongoing second Test against India in Colombo, adding another disciplinary flashpoint to a match that had already been marred by the ugly confrontation between Yashasvi Jaiswal and Asitha Fernando.Jayasuriya was on Tuesday handed an official reprimand and one demerit point for breaching the ICC Code of Conduct during the second day's play of the Colombo Test.The left-arm spinner was found to have breached Article 2.2 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to the âabuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Matchâ.It was Jayasuriya's first offence in a 24-month period, the ICC said.âSri Lanka spinner Prabath Jayasuriya has become the third player to be sanctioned for an incident during the second ICC World Test Championship contest against India after he was hit with an official reprimand following his dismissal in his side's first innings,â the ICC said in a statement.Jayasuriya hits boundary wedges after dismissalThe incident involving Jayasuriya occurred with the final delivery of the second day's play on Monday.The Sri Lanka spinner was adjudged leg-before wicket off India spinner Manav Suthar. As he walked back towards the dressing room following his dismissal, Jayasuriya struck the boundary wedges with his bat.The action led to the charge under Article 2.2, with Jayasuriya subsequently admitting the offence and accepting the sanction proposed by Andy Pycroft of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees.As Jayasuriya accepted the sanction, there was no need for a formal hearing. The charge was levelled by on-field umpires Ahsan Raza and Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid, third umpire Rod Tucker and fourth umpire Prageeth Rambukwella.The one demerit point has now been added to Jayasuriya's disciplinary record.Jaiswal, Fernando were first to be punishedJayasuriya's sanction comes after Jaiswal and Fernando were both punished following their heated exchange on the opening day of the Colombo Test.The incident took place in the 17th over of India's first innings after Fernando dismissed Jaiswal. The India opener walked towards the Sri Lanka pacer and the two exchanged words before Fernando moved his head towards Jaiswal.Jaiswal then leaned in, resulting in their heads making contact.Both players were subsequently fined 25 per cent of their match fees and handed one demerit point each for the altercation.With Jayasuriya now joining Jaiswal and Fernando on the ICC's disciplinary list, three players have been sanctioned during the same Test.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I will continue to play for my father': Saransh Jain gets emotional after India Test debut
articles.summary: Cricket News: Saransh Jain made his Test debut for India against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Sunday, becoming the 320th player to represent the country in Test cricket..
articles.body: Saransh Jain made his Test debut for India against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Sunday, becoming the 320th player to represent the country in Test cricket.The 33-year-old all-rounder came into the team in place of Kuldeep Yadav, but the biggest moment of his day was sharing the achievement with his family, especially his late father, who inspired him to play cricket.âFirst of all, I would like to thank God and after that my family. My father is the closest person to me, so I would tell him first (about making Test debut). I started playing cricket because of him, and I will continue to play for him," Saransh told BCCI after receiving his Test cap.Saransh Jainâs India debut is the result of years of struggle, patience and his father Subodhâs unwavering support.Diagnosed with mouth cancer in 2014, Subodh encouraged Saransh to continue cricket despite his son wanting to quit.After limited Ranji opportunities, Saransh flourished under Chandrakant Pandit, becoming a consistent all-rounder. His strong domestic record finally earned him his long-awaited India call-up.A special cap from JadejaThe occasion became even more meaningful when Ravindra Jadeja presented Saransh with his India cap. Saransh said he was happy to receive it from an experienced all-rounder who could motivate him.âJaddu bhai is a legend and if I am getting the cap from him, it will only benefit me. I am very happy. I wanted to get a cap from an all-rounder who will motivate me. I am an all-rounder myself, so I will try to fulfil my dream," he added.Jadeja also encouraged the debutant to stay relaxed and treat the Test like another First-Class game. He praised Saransh's years of hard work in domestic cricket and India A.âTest cap No. 320, Saransh, well done," Jadeja said. âThe hard work that you have done for so many years in domestic cricket and have performed continuously, be it India A or the Ranji Trophy, I think this is a very important opportunity for you in life."He added, âAs a cricketer, everyone has a dream to represent India and become a Test player. You should enjoy this moment. Donât take pressure at all."READ ALSO: 'I fought cancer to see my son play for India': Saransh Jain's long road to Test cricketJadeja further reminded Saransh that he had already handled tough domestic matches and had the full support of his teammates.âJust like you have performed in so many domestic matches, play like you are playing another First-Class match. You have all the other 14 players with you to support you. Enjoy this moment instead of taking pressure," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Data analysts CricViz answer your questions on successful reviews, hat-tricks, Joe Root and more.
articles.body:
During England's first Test against Pakistan, we asked BBC Sport readers to send statistical questions for our colleagues at CricViz.

Our new feature, Ask CricViz, is here to help and we can reveal the first selection of answers below.

Please note that all stats in Tests are inclusive of the recent Australia v Bangladesh Test in Mackay, but do not include stats from the ongoing Sri Lanka v India Test in Colombo.

âââââââââââââââââââ

Graham, Hastings: Against Pakistan, Josh Tongue took two wickets in two balls but missed out on his hat-trick. What is the 'conversion rate' from having two in two, to going on and getting the hat-trick?

CricViz: In Tests where such data is available in our database, there have been 1,355 occasions where a bowler has taken wickets in two consecutive balls, with only 43 (3.2%) of them converted to a hat-trick.

There have been a total of 49 hat-tricks in Test history but we have the ball-by-ball details for 43 of them.

Across his Test career, Josh Tongue has had two wickets in two balls on four occasions and yet no hat-tricks. The four instances include the two occasions in the last Test versus Pakistan at Headingley, once in the Ashes Test at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in December 2025, and against India at Headingley in June 2025.

Here's another interesting bit: Australia's Mitchell Starc has taken wickets in two consecutive balls on 17 occasions in Tests but is yet to register a hat-trick.

Charles Dennett, Lichfield: When Joe Root was involved in a 50-run partnership with Jordan Cox, it made me think that he must be close to being the player involved in the most 50-run partnerships with the greatest number of distinct batting partners. Is this true?

CricViz: You're spot on with your observation. In the partnership of 150 with Jordan Cox at Headingley, Joe Root has now registered 50-plus run partnerships with 45 distinct partners in Test, the joint-most - tied with Shivnarine Chanderpaul from West Indies.

Also interestingly, that partnership with Jordan Cox was the 88th time Joe Root has been involved in a 100-plus partnership, the joint-most in Test history on par with Rahul Dravid from India.

Harvey, Dartford: After hearing about Ollie Robinson's terrific stats with balls bowled hitting the stumps, can you tell us the bowler (seamer or spinner) who has the highest percentage of their balls bowled that would go on to hit the stumps?

CricViz: In the ball-tracking era (since 2006) former Pakistan all-rounder Mohammad Hafeez has the highest percentage of balls projected to hit the stumps at 41%. When considering only pace bowlers, Paul Collingwood leads the way with just under 19% of his deliveries hitting the stumps.

Tests in Bangladesh have the highest percentage of deliveries hitting the stumps at 27%, no surprise considering the amount of spin bowled. The fast and bouncy pitches of Australia have historically seen just 12% of deliveries hit the stumps, however, the lowest for any nation.

Ben, Llangrannog: Which batter has had the greatest success with decision review system (DRS) reviews?

CricViz: Of the 35 batters to have taken 15 or more reviews in all Tests since the start of 2016, Bangladesh's Liton Das has the highest success rate with 68.8% (11 out of 16) of his DRS reviews overturned by the umpire, followed by India's Cheteshwar Pujara with 60% (9 out of 15) and West Indies' Kraigg Brathwaite with 55.6% (10 out of 18).

If you look at this from a bowler's perspective, of the 58 bowlers to have taken 15 or more reviews in all Tests since the start of 2016, West Indies' Kemar Roach has the highest success rate with 35% (14 out of 40) of his DRS reviews overturned by the umpire, followed by England's Chris Woakes with 29.4% (10 out of 34) and Stuart Broad with 29.1% (16 out of 55).

Jack, Tanzania: If he continues at his current rate, when is Joe Root predicted to beat Tendulkar's run record in Test matches?

CricViz: Joe Root is currently on 14,180 Test runs, 1,741 runs behind Sachin Tendulkar's tally of 15,921. In Tests since the start of 2024, Root has scored 2,794 runs in 32 Tests and 58 innings, scoring 47.6 runs per innings on average. If he continues scoring at the same rate, he will need another 37 innings to go past Tendulkar's run record. That could approximately be around 20 Tests.

As of now, until the end of the next home summer in England, Root has another 14 Tests to go, with two more Tests left in this current series against Pakistan, three away Tests in South Africa in December and January 2027, two away Tests in Bangladesh in February 2027, a one-off 150th Anniversary Test match versus Australia at the MCG in March 2027, followed by one home Test versus Bangladesh at Lord's in May 2027, and the five Ashes Tests in June and August 2027.

It could be 15 Tests until the end of the next summer if England convert their slim chance to qualify for the final of the World Test Championship (WTC).

Current World Test Championship standings

Freddie Davidson, Northampton: Who has the highest average across all formats over the last 10 years, all-format player?

CricViz: Since the start of 2016 in men's internationals, 43 players have scored at least 1,500 runs in men's Tests, 1,000 runs in ODIs and 500 runs in T20Is.

Of these 43 players, Virat Kohli's average of 56.4 is the highest in these last 10 years. Kohli averages 48.3 in Tests, 67.6 in ODIs and 50.3 in T20Is.

Joe Belham, Manchester: Is there any data to prove if left-handed or right-handed batters are better across the history of the sport? Commentators often suggest that left-handed batters are more attractive on the eye and I've always thought that must be nonsense!

CricViz: Looking at this in terms of batting average, in all three international formats in both the men's and women's formats, left-handed batters fare better compared to right-handed batters (if we're looking at just the recognised batters playing in the top seven in the batting order).

Ben Snowball, Surrey: At what specific pace (mph) has there been the most wickets in Test cricket for fast bowlers?

CricViz: In Tests where ball-tracking data is available (since the start of 2006), if we break down all wickets in a 1mph range, deliveries from pace bowlers in the 84-85mph range have seen the most wickets with 1,594 in total. If you break the speeds down to a single decimal, 84.6 mph has been the most productive wicket-taking delivery with 193 wickets in total.

Leo, London: In the wake of Bazball, I would love to see breakdowns of risk/reward for various players and various shots. In general, do you have statistics on outcomes for forward defensives, cuts, drives, hooks, pulls, etc?

CricViz: Looking at the last three years of shot type data against pace in Test cricket, the dismissal rate for some 'attacking' shots is relatively similar to that of defensive strokes, with defensive shots seeing a dismissal every 41 deliveries, similar to that of cut shots (40.4 balls per dismissal) and flicks (38.1 balls per dismissal).

While batters may be striking at 123 when driving, their dismissal rate sits at 31.9, 10 balls lower than that of defensive strokes. Hook (15 balls per dismissal) and pull (22.7 balls per dismissal) shots hover around the 150 mark in terms of strike-rate but with a much more frequent dismissal rate compared to defending.

Batters are dismissed every 295.5 balls when leaving; a good leave is certainly the best shot in the book when it comes to keeping your wicket intact.

Chris Crighton, Stanmore: What ball of the over takes the most wickets? My money is on the sixth!

CricViz: Well, unfortunately it's not the sixth ball, Chris. In Test cricket, the second ball of the over has seen the most wickets fall on 11,866 occasions, followed by the fifth ball with 11,787 wickets. This takes into account Tests with such ball-by-ball data where we've had four balls, five balls and eight balls in an over and now finally settling to the standard six.

Chris, Derbyshire: What is the most common score in Test match cricket (team and individual)?

CricViz: Most common team score in Tests: 296 (44 instances), followed by 191 (43 instances) and then 223 (42 instances).

Most common individual score in Tests: As expected, 0 with 11,877 instances followed by 1 (4,684 instances) and then 4 (3,897 instances). Note that the score of 0 here includes all instances of a batter coming to bat including dismissals and not outs.

Ben, Natland: How many times did Mahendra Singh Dhoni hit a six to win a game? And is he the person to do this the most times?

CricViz: MS Dhoni has hit a six to win an ODI or T20I on 12 occasions, the most by any batter in limited-overs in international cricket.

Most instances to win a game with a six in run-chases in ODIs and T20Is:

CricViz: Since the start of 2016 in men's internationals, 43 players have scored at least 1,500 runs in men's Tests, 1,000 runs in ODIs and 500 runs in T20Is.
Of these 43 players, Virat Kohli's average of 56.4 is the highest in these last 10 years. Kohli averages 48.3 in Tests, 67.6 in ODIs and 50.3 in T20Is.

Joe Belham, Manchester: Is there any data to prove if left-handed or right-handed batters are better across the history of the sport? Commentators often suggest that left-handed batters are more attractive on the eye and I've always thought that must be nonsense!

CricViz: Looking at this in terms of batting average, in all three international formats in both the men's and women's formats, left-handed batters fare better compared to right-handed batters (if we're looking at just the recognised batters playing in the top seven in the batting order).
Ben Snowball, Surrey: At what specific pace (mph) has there been the most wickets in Test cricket for fast bowlers?

CricViz: In Tests where ball-tracking data is available (since the start of 2006), if we break down all wickets in a 1mph range, deliveries from pace bowlers in the 84-85mph range have seen the most wickets with 1,594 in total. If you break the speeds down to a single decimal, 84.6 mph has been the most productive wicket-taking delivery with 193 wickets in total.

Leo, London: In the wake of Bazball, I would love to see breakdowns of risk/reward for various players and various shots. In general, do you have statistics on outcomes for forward defensives, cuts, drives, hooks, pulls, etc?

CricViz: Looking at the last three years of shot type data against pace in Test cricket, the dismissal rate for some 'attacking' shots is relatively similar to that of defensive strokes, with defensive shots seeing a dismissal every 41 deliveries, similar to that of cut shots (40.4 balls per dismissal) and flicks (38.1 balls per dismissal).

Hook (15 balls per dismissal) and pull (22.7 balls per dismissal) shots hover around the 150 mark in terms of strike-rate but with a much more frequent dismissal rate compared to defending.

articles.title: Late-night incidents shaming English cricket: Cook says âJust have some kind of brain cellsâ
articles.summary: Cricket News: Englandâs cricketing culture is under fresh scrutiny after another late-night incident involving one of its players, raising questions over whether th.
articles.body: Englandâs cricketing culture is under fresh scrutiny after another late-night incident involving one of its players, raising questions over whether the traditional post-match drink has gone too far in an era of increasingly professional sport.The latest episode involved fast bowler Brydon Carse, who was pictured outside a nightclub in the early hours of Sunday in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers. The incident came just days after newly appointed England captain Joe Root had called for greater responsibility from the players.The England Cricket Regulator is investigating the matter, putting the spotlight back on the off-field behaviour of the men's squad and prompting questions over whether the team needs another cultural reset.Former England captain Alastair Cook believes the players need to exercise better judgement rather than necessarily abandon socialising altogether.âJust have some kind of brain cells amongst you, seeing what's just gone on,â Cook said on the Stick to Cricket podcast released Tuesday. âSurely someone says either don't go to that place, or at 12 a.m. or 1 a.m. say, 'Let's go and find ourselves somewhere quieter if we want to carry on.âBrookâs club incident set the alarm bells ringingThe concerns are not new. England's problems with late-night behaviour began making headlines during their white-ball tour of New Zealand in October last year.A day before the third and final ODI, captain Harry Brook was hit by a bouncer after being denied entry to a club in Wellington. Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue were also present during the night out.Brook was fined around Â£30,000 and given a final warning, although the sanctions only became public months later.âI want to apologise for my actions,â Brook said. âI fully accept that my behavior was wrong and brought embarrassment to both myself and the England team.âDuckett and Stokes added to growing concernsDuring the Ashes series in Australia, Ben Duckett's night out in Noosa also attracted attention after footage showed the England opener appearing disorientated and telling people he could not remember how to return to his hotel.âI am sorry for that incident, it was not professional and shouldn't have happened,â Duckett later said. âThere is no hiding away from it.âEngland managing director Rob Key subsequently said he would investigate the team's drinking habits.The controversy intensified after England's home Test series against New Zealand. Following victory in the first Test at Lord's, Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson continued celebrations with a night out in London. A member of England's security staff was reportedly struck by a Saracens rugby player during the evening.Stokes and Atkinson were left out of the second Test while the incident was investigated. The investigation ultimately found no âregulatory breachâ, but the episode added to the growing scrutiny surrounding England's off-field culture.Stokes later announced his retirement from international cricket during the third Test, saying the previous few months had âtaken its tollâ. Brendon McCullum was subsequently dismissed as Test coach, while Key said the England and Wales Cricket Board was considering an alcohol ban.Carse incident brings scrutiny backCarse's latest incident technically occurred while he was on domestic duty with Durham rather than with England. He had been released from the England squad to play against Derbyshire after not being selected for the first Test against Pakistan.However, Carse was subsequently retained in the squad for the second Test before being dropped on Monday as the investigation into the incident continued.According to Britain's Press Association, Carse was briefly arrested after the incident. England bowler Matthew Potts was also with him on the night out, while footage circulating on social media showed Stokes watching as Carse was held in handcuffs.The repeated incidents have revived the debate over England's drinking culture, with the central question no longer simply whether players should celebrate after matches, but whether a highly professional sporting setup needs clearer boundaries around how and where those celebrations take place.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: Sarfaraz Khan made a big impact as a substitute fielder for the injured Rishabh Pant on Day 3 of Indiaâs second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo.His .
articles.body: Sarfaraz Khan made a big impact as a substitute fielder for the injured Rishabh Pant on Day 3 of Indiaâs second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo.His constant chatter from short leg appeared to unsettle Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva and wicketkeeper-batter Niroshan Dickwella, with both eventually getting out.Sarfaraz gets under Sri Lanka's skinBefore Manav Suthar bowled to Dhananjaya, the Sri Lankan captain stopped play because of movement behind the bowlerâs arm. Sarfaraz used the moment to distract him, telling him to focus on the ball instead.âNothing is there, bro. You are looking there. You are just wasting time, bro. Don't be scared. You are the captain. Come on, bro," he was heard saying on the stump mic.Watch:âWhy are you worried about that side. Look straight," he added.The tactic seemed to work soon after. Suthar dismissed Dhananjaya in the same over when the batter edged a tossed-up delivery. Dhruv Jurelâs gloves deflected the ball towards slip, where KL Rahul eventually completed the catch. Dhananjaya was out for 8.Dickwella falls into India's trapSarfaraz continued his chatter when Niroshan Dickwella came to the crease. India also used short-pitched deliveries against the wicketkeeper-batter, a strategy that had worked in the first Test.Despite the exchanges being accompanied by smiles, Sarfaraz had the final say when Dickwella gloved a delivery from Mohammed Siraj through to Jurel. His dismissal further strengthened Indiaâs position.Earlier, India declared their first innings at 503/9. Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel scored centuries, while Asitha Fernando was Sri Lankaâs best bowler with four wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brydon Carse: Joe Root says he is 'hacked off' and 'disappointed' at nightclub incident
articles.summary: England captain Joe Root says he is "hacked off" and "disappointed" at the incident involving fast bowler Brydon Carse at a Derby nightclub.
articles.body:
England captain Joe Root says he is "hacked off" and "disappointed" at the incident involving fast bowler Brydon Carse at a Derby nightclub.

Carse, 31, was dropped from the squad for the second Test starting against Pakistan this week.

Images that appeared on social media on Sunday showed Carse in handcuffs outside a bar in Derby on Saturday night and he was briefly arrested and subsequently de-arrested.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off, I'm really disappointed," Root said in the opening to a news conference.

"After last week's performance, we're sat here and we're talking about something that is not related to it at all."

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has referred the incident to the Cricket Regulator and Carse was replaced in the squad by Sonny Baker, with the Test starting at Lord's on Thursday.

Carse was not on England duty at the time of the incident as he was released to play for Durham, but he is a centrally contracted player.

Root also said he had spoken to his England team-mate about the incident, and expressed his frustration at the "stupid mistakes" that are continually being made.

"I've spoken to Brydon, and when I first found out my main concern was him as a person," Root added.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn by saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure that when he gets his chance he will say that himself.

"But I don't think it's the isolated incident itself, it's the fact we keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

In October, England white-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer outside a nightclub in Wellington, New Zealand, with team-mates Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue also present.

During the Ashes tour of Australia, opener Ben Duckett was filmed apparently drunk on England's holiday in Noosa.

And in June, former Test captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and were present when a member of England's security staff was punched by a Saracens rugby player in a London nightclub.

In this latest incident, Carse was with Durham team-mates Stokes and Matthew Potts, all of whom are under England central contracts. In Stokes' case, the England deal remains in place despite his international retirement in June.

It makes a total of eight contracted players who have been involved in or present for late-night incidents in the past year â more than a quarter of the 30 men on England deals.

Punishment to send a shiver needed - Vaughan Published 1 day ago

Punishment to send a shiver needed - Vaughan

England drop Carse after nightclub incident & Pakistan's struggles

When he was reappointed as Test captain, Root confirmed he would remove the midnight curfew which was previously in place during Stokes and Brendon McCullum's regime after a string of off-field incidents during the Ashes over the winter.

Root stood by that decision, saying he still did not think it was "the right way to go", but admitted it would take some time for the team to be trusted by the fans again.

"In many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back, and it's something that we're going to have to live and breathe consistently," he said.

"I might only be in this dressing room for a couple more years, but there is a group of players there who might be in there for another 10.

"We've had a very strong discussion about what's expected of everyone when they play for England, what the standards are that we have to uphold, not just on the field but off it.

"I've made it very clear how we want to conduct ourselves, and now we've got to live it and show people what I see day in, day out in the dressing room, which is a group of characters who know what it means to play for England and not having incidents define how we are seen as players. That's going to take some work and time."

Root also confirmed he had spoken to his predecessor Stokes, who was also seen in the social media video, but only to check in on Carse's wellbeing.

He was asked what potential consequences Carse might face but said he would have no involvement as it is in the hands of the regulator, and was keen to reiterate that he was focusing on moving forward and "building something to be proud of".

"I don't think the recent past has been a good look," Root, 35, said.

"It's our responsibility to change that. I see the dressing room every day and how we operate around cricket and it's very impressive.

"But at the same time, I can understand why we are viewed in a certain way and in a certain light at the moment.

"That's what lies ahead of us, to change that. I just think, if we don't put ourselves in certain situations, it's not something we will have to worry about."

'Impressive Root shows he is the leader England need'

If there was any question as to why England turned to Joe Root for a second stint as Test captain, if he is the right man for the job, then this address at Lord's removed all of those doubts.

Root showed himself to be the leader England need in this moment. Clearly ticking over what happened at the weekend, Root was able to strike the balance between letting his feelings be known, showing compassion for Brydon Carse and not pre-judging the investigation that is ongoing.

There have been plenty of these kinds of news conferences over the past year: someone wearing an England badge explaining a misdemeanour, promising to do better. This time, when Root spoke, his words were plausible and believable.

Some wondered why Root was the one left to face the media, rather than members of the management team like director of cricket Rob Key or chief executive Richard Gould.

Maybe it is because no-one else was able to speak with Root's gravitas. No-one in a suit, not Ben Stokes, nor Harry Brook. Perhaps this is the most impressive display of leadership anyone connected with English cricket has shown for some time.

It should leave no one â especially not the England players â in any doubt where their captain stands on this issue. For any athlete to tell the world they are "hacked off" with a team-mate is a stark message.

Root addressed his England team on Tuesday morning. If the captain was able to speak like this in public, one can only wonder about the sternness of the message delivered in private. Carse would not have been there, but plenty of others who have erred in the past year would have been in the room.

There will be no return for the midnight curfew, but Root was also quite clear about players avoiding situations that could lead to trouble. "Stupid mistakes", he called them. He hammered home the point that players will not find trouble if they do not put themselves in the places where trouble could find them.

But Root also regularly mentioned the notion of this team now having an opportunity to build something on and off the field. Put simply, their reputation in the eyes of the public cannot get much lower, so the only direction is improvement.

Amid all the controversy, English cricket is fortunate to have Root. Not only is he a bona fide all-time great, but also a superb example of how all sportspeople should go about their business on and off the field.

Last week, before his first Test back in charge, Root asked his players to be "good role models and good human beings". They should look no further than their captain for inspiration.

Root stood by that decision, saying he still did not think it was "the right way to go", but admitted it would take some time for the team to be trusted by the fans again.

"In many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back, and it's something that we're going to have to live and breathe consistently," he said.

"I might only be in this dressing room for a couple more years, but there is a group of players there who might be in there for another 10.

"We've had a very strong discussion about what's expected of everyone when they play for England, what the standards are that we have to uphold, not just on the field but off it.

"I've made it very clear how we want to conduct ourselves, and now we've got to live it and show people what I see day in, day out in the dressing room, which is a group of characters who know what it means to play for England and not having incidents define how we are seen as players. That's going to take some work and time."

Root also confirmed he had spoken to his predecessor Stokes, who was also seen in the social media video, but only to check in on Carse's wellbeing.

He was asked what potential consequences Carse might face but said he would have no involvement as it is in the hands of the regulator, and was keen to reiterate that he was focusing on moving forward and "building something to be proud of".

"I don't think the recent past has been a good look," Root, 35, said.

"It's our responsibility to change that. I see the dressing room every day and how we operate around cricket and it's very impressive.

"But at the same time, I can understand why we are viewed in a certain way and in a certain light at the moment.

"That's what lies ahead of us, to change that. I just think, if we don't put ourselves in certain situations, it's not something we will have to worry about."

'Impressive Root shows he is the leader England need'

If there was any question as to why England turned to Joe Root for a second stint as Test captain, if he is the right man for the job, then this address at Lord's removed all of those doubts.

Root showed himself to be the leader England need in this moment. Clearly ticking over what happened at the weekend, Root was able to strike the balance between letting his feelings be known, showing compassion for Brydon Carse and not pre-judging the investigation that is ongoing.

There have been plenty of these kinds of news conferences over the past year: someone wearing an England badge explaining a misdemeanour, promising to do better. This time, when Root spoke, his words were plausible and believable.

Some wondered why Root was the one left to face the media, rather than members of the management team like director of cricket Rob Key or chief executive Richard Gould.

Maybe it is because no-one else was able to speak with Root's gravitas. No-one in a suit, not Ben Stokes, nor Harry Brook. Perhaps this is the most impressive display of leadership anyone connected with English cricket has shown for some time.

It should leave no one â especially not the England players â in any doubt where their captain stands on this issue. For any athlete to tell the world they are "hacked off" with a team-mate is a stark message.

Root addressed his England team on Tuesday morning. If the captain was able to speak like this in public, one can only wonder about the sternness of the message delivered in private. Carse would not have been there, but plenty of others who have erred in the past year would have been in the room.

There will be no return for the midnight curfew, but Root was also quite clear about players avoiding situations that could lead to trouble. "Stupid mistakes", he called them. He hammered home the point that players will not find trouble if they do not put themselves in the places where trouble could find them.

But Root also regularly mentioned the notion of this team now having an opportunity to build something on and off the field. Put simply, their reputation in the eyes of the public cannot get much lower, so the only direction is improvement.

Amid all the controversy, English cricket is fortunate to have Root. Not only is he a bona fide all-time great, but also a superb example of how all sportspeople should go about their business on and off the field.

Last week, before his first Test back in charge, Root asked his players to be "good role models and good human beings". They should look no further than their captain for inspiration.
paragraphs: England captain Joe Root says he is "hacked off" and "disappointed" at the incident involving fast bowler Brydon Carse at a Derby nightclub.
Carse, 31, was dropped from the squad for the second Test starting against Pakistan this week.
Images that appeared on social media on Sunday showed Carse in handcuffs outside a bar in Derby on Saturday night and he was briefly arrested and subsequently de-arrested.
"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off, I'm really disappointed," Root said in the opening to a news conference.
"After last week's performance, we're sat here and we're talking about something that is not related to it at all."
The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has referred the incident to the Cricket Regulator and Carse was replaced in the squad by Sonny Baker, with the Test starting at Lord's on Thursday.
Carse was not on England duty at the time of the incident as he was released to play for Durham, but he is a centrally contracted player.
Root also said he had spoken to his England team-mate about the incident, and expressed his frustration at the "stupid mistakes" that are continually being made.
"I've spoken to Brydon, and when I first found out my main concern was him as a person," Root added.
"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn by saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure that when he gets his chance he will say that himself.
"But I don't think it's the isolated incident itself, it's the fact we keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."
In October, England white-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer outside a nightclub in Wellington, New Zealand, with team-mates Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue also present.
During the Ashes tour of Australia, opener Ben Duckett was filmed apparently drunk on England's holiday in Noosa.

And in June, former Test captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and were present when a member of England's security staff was punched by a Saracens rugby player in a London nightclub.

In this latest incident, Carse was with Durham team-mates Stokes and Matthew Potts, all of whom are under England central contracts. In Stokes' case, the England deal remains in place despite his international retirement in June.
It makes a total of eight contracted players who have been involved in or present for late-night incidents in the past year â more than a quarter of the 30 men on England deals.

articles.title: 2nd Test: India struggle to finish off tail as Sonal Dinusha, Pasindu Sooriyabandara lead Sri Lanka resistance
articles.summary: Cricket News: India missed several chances to finish off Sri Lanka on Day 3 of the second Test as the hostsâ lower order put up a strong fight in Colombo.Led by Son.
articles.body: India missed several chances to finish off Sri Lanka on Day 3 of the second Test as the hostsâ lower order put up a strong fight in Colombo.Led by Sonal Dinusha and Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Sri Lanka ended the day at 265/8, still 38 runs short of avoiding the follow-on.Sri Lanka's lower order stands firmDinusha remained unbeaten on 85 when rain and bad light brought play to an early close, while Lahiru Kumara was not out on 8. Dinusha continued his excellent run in the series, registering his third score above 50 in as many innings. He battled Indiaâs pace and spin for 201 minutes and refused to give the bowlers an opening.He first added 57 runs with Keshara Nuwantha for the eighth wicket and then put on another 35 with Kumara. The long resistance from Sri Lankaâs tail frustrated India, who have struggled against lower-order batters in the past.Earlier, India appeared in control after reducing Sri Lanka to 216/7 by tea. Manav Suthar dismissed captain Dhananjaya de Silva, who edged to KL Rahul, while Ravindra Jadeja removed Sooriyabandara for a well-made 80. Mohammed Siraj then dismissed Niroshan Dickwella, caught behind by Dhruv Jurel.Sooriyabandara, Mendis give Sri Lanka hopeSri Lanka had begun the day at 8/2 and quickly lost Kamil Mishara for 19, but Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis changed the momentum with an 87-run partnership. Sooriyabandara, playing only his second Test, scored his maiden Test fifty from 76 balls and showed impressive composure.Mendis also attacked the Indian spinners, hitting Suthar for a six, before Prasidh Krishna ended the partnership by getting him to pull a short delivery straight to Jadeja.Despite India regaining control in the middle session, Dinusha and the lower order ensured Sri Lanka finished strongly. With 38 runs still needed to avoid the follow-on, India will hope to wrap up the innings quickly on Day 4.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: âBadly bruisedâ: Morne Morkel reveals why Rishabh Pant did not keep as Dhruv Jurel took gloves
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has revealed that Rishabh Pant's shoulder is âbadly bruisedâ after the wicketkeeper-batter missed wicketke.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has revealed that Rishabh Pant's shoulder is âbadly bruisedâ after the wicketkeeper-batter missed wicketkeeping duties on Day 3 in the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo.Pant suffered the injury on the opening day after taking a blow to his wrist and was forced to retire hurt. He returned on Day 2 and scored a brisk 63 off 89 balls, but did not take the field after India declared their first innings at 503 for nine.Dhruv Jurel, who scored a century on the second day, continued behind the stumps on Tuesday as Pant was kept away from the rigours of wicketkeeping as a precaution.âRishabh Pantâs shoulder is badly bruised. He will be assessed overnight, we want his experience behind the stumps because he reads the game really well,â Morkel said at the post-day press conference.Morkel backs Prasidh, praises SirajPant's injury update came after India's bowlers were unable to finish off Sri Lanka on Day 3. The hosts reached 265 for eight before rain and bad light forced early stumps, with Sonal Dinusha unbeaten on 85.Morkel was particularly pleased with the character shown by Prasidh Krishna, who produced two lively spells and helped India regain momentum during the day.âShows character of Prasidh Krishnaâ¦ guy who had media and commentators on his back. As a team and management we knew about the potential, for him it was about silencing those voices. He lets go of thoughts, loves bowling, does homework and research. Massive student of the game. Has potential and talent to play all formats for a very long time.âHe also praised Mohammed Siraj for his relentless effort on a difficult surface.âSiraj is a guy you want in your team. He can bowl all day from one end with a sore body. Even today, in flat conditions. He kept running in and has been the key guy for us. Quite lucky to have him in the team. Prasidh has extra pace and bounce. We need to use him in phasesâ¦ it can be risky. The whole team is behind him and supporting him even when results don't go his way. It's my job to talk through these things and give him confidenceâ¦âIndia eye quick finish to enforce follow-onSri Lanka resumed from 8 for two but recovered through Pasindu Sooriyabandara's 80 and a series of lower-order partnerships. Dinusha then held firm for 201 minutes, adding 57 with Keshara Nuwantha and an unbeaten 35 with Lahiru Kumara.Sri Lanka still need 38 runs to avoid the follow-on after India posted 503 for nine.Morkel acknowledged the challenge posed by the home side's tail and stressed the importance of maintaining pressure after breakthroughs.âTest cricket is a grind. Tough conditions, hard conditions. The ball goes soft, it was a proper day of Test cricket. We always talk about bowling in partnerships and in pressure. Fun is to breakthrough and then how well you can start again. Follow-on will be Indiaâs first target, we want to get those wickets quickly and be brave and put them in again,â Morne Morkel said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: First in 48 years! Sonal Dinusha joins Zaheer Abbas, Everton Weekes in rare Test feat against India
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha has entered an elite group of batters after becoming only the third player to score 80 or more in each of his fir.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha has entered an elite group of batters after becoming only the third player to score 80 or more in each of his first three Test innings against India, joining West Indies great Everton Weekes and Pakistan legend Zaheer Abbas.Dinusha reached the landmark during a stubborn innings on the third day of the second Test in Colombo, remaining unbeaten on 85 as Sri Lanka finished at 265 for eight after rain and bad light forced an early close.The 25-year-old left-hander had already made 100 and 84 in his first two Test innings against India, and his latest effort made him the first batter since Abbas in 1978 to achieve the feat.Abbas had scored 176, 96 and 235 not out in his first three innings against India, while Weekes made 128, 194 and 162 in 1948. Weekes went on to score centuries in each of his first four innings against India before being dismissed for 90 in his fifth.Dinusha's remarkable start against IndiaDinusha's latest innings also gave him a third consecutive 50-plus score against India, making him only the second Sri Lankan batter and 10th overall to achieve that feat in his first three Test innings against the opposition.The only Sri Lankan to previously accomplish it was Duleep Mendis, who scored 105, 105 and 51 in his first three Test innings against India.Dinusha's performance has been particularly striking given his comfort against spin. He has scored 106 runs through sweep shots â including conventional, slog and reverse sweeps â in the ongoing series, the most by a batter against spin in a Test series since ball-by-ball data became available in 2007 for the relevant shots.Joe Root holds the overall record in the category, having scored 160 runs through sweeps against Sri Lanka in 2021. Ben Duckett has 112 against Pakistan in 2022, while Root scored 106 against India in 2021.Dinusha has taken the sweep to another level in his short Test career. Of his 284 runs against spin, 122 â or 42.95 per cent â have come through sweep shots. He has scored those runs at a remarkable strike rate of 169.44, hitting 11 fours and four sixes without being dismissed playing the shot.Dinusha frustrates India as lower order digs inIndia appeared to be closing in on Sri Lanka's innings when the hosts resumed after tea at 216 for seven. Instead, Dinusha continued to frustrate the attack for 201 minutes.He first added 57 runs with Keshara Nuwantha for the eighth wicket before putting on an unbeaten 35 with Lahiru Kumara for the ninth. Nuwantha faced 74 deliveries, while Kumara survived for 65 minutes off 50 balls.Earlier, India had claimed four wickets for 86 runs in the middle session after Sri Lanka had added 122 in the morning. Manav Suthar dismissed Dhananjaya de Silva, Ravindra Jadeja removed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for 80 and Mohammed Siraj accounted for Niroshan Dickwella.But Dinusha's resistance ensured Sri Lanka remained alive at 265 for eight, still 238 runs behind India's 503 for nine and 38 runs short of avoiding the follow-on.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs Sri Lanka: The good, old grind takes centrestage in Colombo
articles.summary: Cricket News: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: The setting during the final hour resembled that of the second day. The sky suddenly darkened, and the ground staff took .
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: The setting during the final hour resembled that of the second day. The sky suddenly darkened, and the ground staff took position as grey clouds began to gather over the stadium. As the end of the third day drew near and the teams walked off the field, never to return, the feeling was familiar, yet somehow different.On both days, Sri Lanka were in survival mode, but on Tuesday, they kept India on the field for the entire day. The visitors dragged themselves along with slumped shoulders as they toiled for over 80 overs and will have to pick themselves up again for what looks like more hard work to enforce the follow-on. And then put on a brave face for the win."That'll be first prize if we can get those two wickets tomorrow early," said Morkel when asked about the team's thinking regarding enforcing the follow-on."With the weather around and sometimes the time it takes with taking the covers on and off, you know, we want to try and get as many overs as possible," added India's bowling coach.India had the ideal start on a very hot morning when Prasidh Krishna removed Kamil Mishra. Between the overs, the lanky fast bowler would often go down, holding his knees and catching that extra breath, but Shubman Gill never left his ear. The captain's usage of Krishna was enough to understand his reading of the pitch and why he felt that the Karnataka bowler was going to be the key on this surface with the extra bounce. This was the same bounce the opposition pair of Lahiru Kumara and Asitha Fernando used to their advantage on the first two days.Even in short bursts, the fast bowlers found the conditions and the flat track hard work, but Krishna ran in hard to create opportunities for his captain. It wasn't a surprise that Krishna took the second wicket in the morning session. He was rewarded for his persistent and consistent planning. After seeing the passage of play where every wicket came at a premium, the day also saw a period where two wickets fell in as many minutes off deliveries that shouldn't have taken wickets.Pasindu Sooriyabandara played one Ravindra Jadeja ball back onto his own stumps, and Niroshan Dickwella edged an innocuous Mohammed Siraj delivery down the leg side to Dhruv Jurel. Within the space of three deliveries, Sri Lanka were seven down with the scoreboard reading 173, and panic would have triggered in the home dressing room. They had been sitting with their feet up at 122/3 close to Lunch.Key message is whenever we're playing Test cricket, it is a grind. As the boys walked in there, I said to them that it was a proper day of Test cricket, and this is how we're going to learn.There were plenty of oohs and aahs between those two events, but India were made to work hard. The odd ball gripped, a fair few turned, but Sri Lanka adeptly countered the challenge posed by the trio of Manav Suthar, Ravindra Jadeja and Saransh Jain. India let the game drift away with open fields in the second session and then towards the end when Sonal Dinusha frustrated the visitors with the tail.The tail came back to sting India, again, but it hurt the most on Tuesday as it didn't allow India another crack at Sri Lanka in fading light. For most of that period, the attention focused on getting rid of Lahiru, while Sonal continued his ways in a rather comfortable and open field setting. Result: They have already survived over 15 overs and look in no mood to throw their wickets away.For Morkel, it was a tough day of Test cricket, and he feels this experience will build character within the team for bigger challenges."Key message is whenever we're playing Test cricket, it is a grind. As the boys walked in there, I said to them that it was a proper day of Test cricket, and this is how we're going to learn. We always talk about bowling and partnerships. articles.title: âReally hacked offâ: Carse in handcuffs leaves Root âreally disappointedâ as England face fresh scrutiny
articles.summary: Cricket News: England captain Joe Root has admitted he is âreally hacked offâ and âreally disappointedâ after another off-field incident involving an England player.
articles.body: England captain Joe Root has admitted he is âreally hacked offâ and âreally disappointedâ after another off-field incident involving an England player brought the team's drinking culture under scrutiny again.Root's comments came after fast bowler Brydon Carse was pictured outside a nightclub in the early hours of Sunday in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers. The incident has prompted an investigation by England's Cricket Regulator and reignited questions over the team's conduct away from the field.The latest episode is particularly awkward for Root, who had only recently spoken about the responsibilities that come with representing England after the team leadership scrapped a midnight curfew imposed following a string of controversial late-night incidents.âUltimately youâre grown adults,â Root had said after the curfew was removed. âYou know what it takes to play for England, you know what your responsibilities are off the field, and we need to make sure we donât find ourselves with any little situations off the field.âRoot admits frustration over repeated incidentsThe latest incident appears to have tested Root's patience.âIf Iâm being brutally honest, Iâm really hacked off. Iâm really disappointed,â Root said at a news conference on Tuesday.âItâs not the isolated incident itself,â Root added. âItâs the fact we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and itâs detracting from what weâre doing on the field.âCarse has yet to publicly comment on the incident, but Root said the fast bowler was deeply remorseful.âHeâs very upset, has been very apologetic, and understands his actions.âRoot was also blunt about the wider picture surrounding England's recent off-field episodes.âI donât think it has been a very good look, the recent past, if Iâm being brutally honest,â Root said. âAt all.âFrom post-match beers to cultural resetThe scrutiny comes despite the long-standing tradition of players sharing drinks after matches. Former England captain Ben Stokes himself spoke about the importance of celebrating with teammates after England's win over New Zealand at Lord's in June.âI probably wonât be real happy and smiley,â Stokes said at the time, âuntil I get up there and share a proper beer with the boys.âBut a series of incidents has raised questions about where celebration ends and irresponsible behaviour begins.Former England captain Alastair Cook offered a blunt assessment on the Stick to Cricket podcast.âJust have some kind of brain cells amongst you, seeing whatâs just gone on,â Cook said. âSurely someone says either donât go to that place, or at 12 a.m. or 1 a.m. say, 'Letâs go and find ourselves somewhere quieter if we want to carry on.âGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Joe Root: Furious England captain 'hacked off' after Brydon Carse incident overshadows Pakistan victory
articles.summary: Joe Root "hacked off" by "stupid mistakes" as off-field controversy involving Brydon Carse overshadows his successful return as Test captain; watch the second England vs Pakistan Test live on Sky Sports from Thursday
articles.body:
A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.

England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.

Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

  • England without Carse for Lord's Test after nightclub incident
  • With alarm bells ringing, what's gone wrong for Pakistan cricket?
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream no contract

Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.

"In terms of the incident itself, obviously with the regulator, there's not a lot I can say on it. It's in their hands now.

"I've spoken to Brydon when I first found out; my first concern was for him as a person. In my time in the dressing room, you obviously develop personal relationships with players.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn when I say he's been very upset and has been very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

"It's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact that we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

'We have to earn a lot of trust back'

Asked if English cricket had an image problem, Root, who previously called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, said: "We have an opportunity going forward.

"Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.

"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.

"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.

"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen [Fleming], and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."

Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.

"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.

"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.

"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

Watch day one of the second Test between England and Pakistan, at Lord's, live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 10am Thursday (11am first ball). Stream with NOW.

England vs Pakistan Test series schedule

All games live on Sky Sports; all 11am starts UK and Ireland

  • First Test (Headingley) - England won by innings and 103 runs
  • Second Test (Lord's) - August 27-31
  • Third Test (Edgbaston) - September 9-13

articles.title: âIncredibly emotionalâ: Anaya Bangar gets Cricket Australia nod for elite womenâs cricket, eyes WBBL
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has taken a major step towards returning to competitive cricket after Cricket Australia confirmed that she will be eligible to.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has taken a major step towards returning to competitive cricket after Cricket Australia confirmed that she will be eligible to play elite womenâs cricket in the country from March 2027.Bangar, who underwent gender-affirming surgery in March, received the confirmation under Cricket Australiaâs Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy. The decision opens a pathway for her to pursue a place in the Womenâs Big Bash League (WBBL), although she stressed that eligibility does not guarantee a franchise contract.In an exclusive conversation with Bombay Times, Anaya, daughter of former India all-rounder and batting coach Sanjay Bangar, described the development as an emotional moment after fearing that her cricket career had ended following her transition.âI am now eligible to play in the Womenâs Big Bash League (WBBL) in Australia from March 2027 onwards. For me, this is incredibly emotional because there was a point when I genuinely believed I had lost cricket forever,â she told Bombay Times.âCricket has been such a fundamental part of my identity since childhood, and having to step away from the sport after my transition was one of the hardest things I experienced. So this isnât simply about being included in a womenâs league. It represents the possibility of returning to the sport I deeply love,â she said.Eligibility secured, but WBBL place must still be earnedAnaya was quick to clarify that Cricket Australiaâs decision only provides her with the opportunity to pursue elite womenâs cricket. She will still have to earn a place in a WBBL squad through her performances.âCricket Australia has allowed me to pursue elite womenâs cricket in Australia. The next challenge is to get myself into the best possible physical and competitive shape and put myself in a position to be considered by a WBBL franchise. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,â she said.She explained that the WBBLâs overseas-player contracting and draft system means she will have to convince a franchise of her value.âThe WBBL has an overseas-player contracting and draft system, where clubs select from the pool of available international players, like it happens in the IPL or the WPL,â Anaya said.âSo ultimately, I still have to convince a franchise that I can contribute to their team. For me, that means getting back into competitive cricket in Australian leagues, working on my batting, bowling, fielding and fitness, training consistently and demonstrating that I can perform at that level.âFrom uncertainty to a pathway in AustraliaThe development comes against the backdrop of different policies governing transgender participation in cricket.Cricket Australia has a different framework for elite domestic cricket, allowing transgender women who meet its eligibility and testosterone-related criteria to participate.Anaya said she had hoped for a clearer pathway in India but eventually chose to focus on what she could control.âWhen you grow up playing cricket competitively, the idea of potentially never being able to play again is incredibly difficult,â she said.âBut Iâve also learned that I canât build my future around waiting for somebody else to make a decision. I had to focus on what I could control â my health, my transition, my performance, the scientific evidence, and having conversations with sporting organisations.âShe added: âIâm grateful that I have a pathway in Australia, and I hope that my journey can contribute to a broader conversation about how sporting bodies can approach transgender participation with both fairness and inclusion.âCricket Australiaâs eligibility confirmation said Anayaâs determination to commence in March 2027 would not be affected by amendments to its policy. It also confirmed that she is currently eligible to participate in Premier Cricket competitions in any Australian state or territory.For Anaya, the ambition is ultimately straightforward: âI would love to reach a point where Iâm simply another cricketer competing against some of the best players in the world.âGet the latest Sports News and Live updates.
